summary.short: As introduced, this bill would direct the Federal Trade Commission to require covered entities deploying machine-learning or AI-based algorithms for consequential decisions to perform impact assessments and submit summary reports, and would make violations unlawful. Regulations due two years after enactment.
summary.long: As introduced, the bill would direct the Federal Trade Commission to promulgate regulations, within two years after enactment, requiring covered entities to perform impact assessments of covered algorithms before and after deployment and to submit summary reports to the Commission. A covered algorithm is a computational process derived from machine learning, natural language processing, AI or similar techniques that, for a consequential action, creates content, affects information delivery, makes a decision or facilitates human decision making. Covered entities are persons under Commission jurisdiction that deploy such algorithms and meet receipts, equity-value or identifying-information thresholds. Assessments must address listed matters, including stakeholder consultation, privacy risks, differential performance, input data and consumer rights. Covered entities must disclose their status to persons that sell, license or otherwise provide the algorithm, and the Commission must publish annual reports and a public repository of summary report information. Violations, and knowing substantial assistance to them, are unlawful and treated as unfair or deceptive practices under the FTC Act; state attorneys general may bring civil actions. The bill creates a Bureau of Technology within the Commission and does not preempt state, tribal, city or local law.

notes: Introduced bill, text as introduced; no enacted or amended text. It does not amend, repeal or implement any existing instrument, and no legal_basis relation is stated. Target instrument IDs are null because registry IDs were not supplied. Internal points: the Sec. 3(a)(2) heading reads 'Preemption of private contracts' but the text makes the Sec. 3(a)(1) acts unlawful regardless of agreements; Sec. 11 separately states the Act does not preempt State or local law. Sec. 5(a)(2) and 2(6) cite the FTC Act, not this Act. Sec. 2(6)(A)(i) and (ii) set two different dollar tiers for covered-entity status. Sec. 3(b)(3) makes the regulations effective 2 years after promulgation, while Sec. 3(b)(1) requires promulgation within 2 years of enactment, so the effective date depends on promulgation timing.
